title: What Anthropic’s record $81 billion IPO means for Gulf investors
author: Samuel Wendel
text:
Explainer

What Anthropic’s record $81 billion IPO means for Gulf investors

The creator of the Claude chatbot has raised $81.3 billion in the world's largest IPO, and Gulf investors have emerged as major players.

Samuel Wendel

Anthropic billboards are displayed in Times Square as shares begin trading after their IPO on Nov. 19, 2026, in New York City. — Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images

Anthropic is set to debut on Nasdaq on Thursday after the creator of the Claude chatbot raised $81.3 billion from the largest initial public offering in history. Key Gulf investors are among the potential winners from this bellwether moment for the artificial intelligence boom even as concerns mount about unsustainable spending, security and safety risks. What happened: Anthropic priced its offering of 980 million shares at $83 each on Wednesday, above its initial $70-$78 range, in a transaction valuing the six-year-old AI lab at roughly $1.5 trillion. A separate $26 billion private placement took the combined deal above $107 billion.Anthropic will become the first major frontier AI developer to go public while delivering the largest offering on record, eclipsing SpaceX’s $75 billion IPO in June.The San Francisco-based company counts backers including Abu Dhabi’s state-linked AI investment fund MGX and the Qatar Investment Authority. The first notable regional investor to snap up an Anthropic stake was Dubai property tycoon Hussain Sajwani’s Damac Group, which also bought about $50 million of shares held by bankrupt crypto exchange FTX in July 2024.
